description:
Zero Boundaries is my solo team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. I'm a Computer Science and Engineering student passionate about software development, open source, and space science. 

Through FireSignal, I combined satellite data analysis with interactive web technologies to make Earth's fire activity patterns easier to explore and understand. Zero Boundaries reflects my curiosity, creativity, and belief in exploring ideas without limits.
summary:
FireSignal is an interactive scientific platform that helps people explore and understand patterns in satellite-detected fire activity across India.

Using NASA FIRMS observations from MODIS (2003–2025) and VIIRS (2013–2025), FireSignal transforms satellite detections into comparable geographic and temporal indicators. Its Geographic Observatory enables exploration of fire activity across India's states and union territories, while historical visualizations reveal seasonal patterns and long-term changes.

A central challenge is that MODIS and VIIRS have different detection capabilities, making their raw observation counts unsuitable for direct comparison. FireSignal addresses this through a common 5 km equal-area grid, occupied grid-cell-day measurements, and empirically evaluated statistical harmonization methods.

The platform also includes an interactive Sensor Laboratory and transparent research methodology, allowing users to investigate how satellite characteristics affect observations.

FireSignal makes complex Earth observation data more accessible for research, education, and environmental analysis while clearly communicating scientific uncertainties and limitations.
details:
The Problem

Satellite observations provide valuable evidence of fire activity, but interpreting them is not straightforward. Different instruments detect thermal anomalies at different spatial resolutions, viewing geometries, and sensitivities. Consequently, increases in satellite detections do not necessarily indicate equivalent increases in actual fire occurrence.

This is particularly important when comparing historical MODIS observations with newer VIIRS observations.

Our Solution

FireSignal is an interactive research application designed to make satellite-detected fire activity across India easier to explore, compare, and interpret.

The platform combines four interconnected experiences:

  1. Geographic Observatory: Explore satellite-detected activity across India's 36 states and union territories using interactive geographic visualizations, regional comparisons, and historical indicators.
  2. Historical Patterns: Examine temporal trends, seasonal variation, and differences between MODIS and VIIRS observations. The Historical Patterns view also provides a unified 2003–2025 burning-activity calendar, combining observed MODIS indicators (2003–2012) with statistically harmonized VIIRS indicators (2013–2025), alongside sensor provenance, seasonal anomalies, and downloadable monthly data.
  3. Sensor Laboratory: Investigate how satellite sensor characteristics influence the interpretation of fire detections.
  4. Research Methods: Understand the underlying data, calculations, harmonization methods, and scientific limitations.

How It Works

FireSignal processes historical NASA FIRMS active-fire observations from MODIS Terra/Aqua (2003–2025) and VIIRS Suomi-NPP (2013–2025).

Rather than treating every satellite detection as an independent fire, the analytical pipeline projects observations onto a common 5 km equal-area grid (EPSG:6933) and computes occupied grid-cell-days (OGCD). This measures how frequently grid cells contain satellite detections across time.

For the overlapping sensor period, FireSignal evaluates statistical harmonization methods to investigate differences between MODIS and VIIRS observations. These models are assessed using time-separated training, validation, and testing periods.

The resulting datasets power an interactive web application.

Technologies Used

  • React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts for the interactive frontend.
  • Python for scientific data processing, aggregation, and statistical analysis.
  • GeoJSON and geographic projection methods for regional visualization.
  • NASA FIRMS active-fire observations from MODIS and VIIRS.
  • geoBoundaries administrative boundary data for geographic context.
  • GitHub for open-source development and Vercel for deployment.

Innovation and Creativity

FireSignal goes beyond plotting satellite hotspots. Its distinguishing feature is the integration of historical geographic exploration with explicit treatment of differences between satellite sensors.

The project combines a common spatial measurement framework, empirical cross-sensor comparison, regional analysis, and interactive explanations of scientific uncertainty.

Instead of presenting raw detection totals as definitive fire counts, FireSignal encourages users to distinguish observations from physical events.

Intended Impact

FireSignal aims to make satellite-derived fire information more accessible to students, researchers, educators, and environmental analysts.

It can support exploratory research into regional and seasonal fire-activity patterns and help users understand the strengths and limitations of Earth observation systems.

FireSignal is not an emergency warning service, a burned-area measurement system, or a substitute for verified ground observations. Its purpose is scientific exploration, education, and transparent interpretation of satellite evidence.

Open Science and Reproducibility

The project's source code, methodology, software license, and third-party attribution notices are publicly available. Scientific assumptions and evaluation procedures are documented so that others can inspect the analytical approach and build upon the work.
